name: What happens if my remodel uncovers noncompliant electrical or plumbing?

mainEntity.name: What happens if my remodel in Burbank or Pasadena uncovers old electrical or plumbing that does not meet current standards?
mainEntity.text: What happens if my remodel in Burbank or Pasadena uncovers old electrical or plumbing that does not meet current standards?

acceptedAnswer.text: This is one of the most common surprises in older homes. Once walls or floors are opened, the team may find old wiring, undersized panels, corroded piping, unsafe connections, or prior work that was never properly finished. When that happens, the project usually cannot continue as planned until the problem is corrected. The fix may be limited to the affected area, or it may require broader system upgrades if the issue is widespread. Homeowners should expect the contractor to document the condition, explain the correction, and show whether the change affects permits or inspection timing. The best protection is a thorough preconstruction evaluation and a contingency budget so the project does not stall when hidden conditions appear.
acceptedAnswer.description: If a remodel uncovers outdated electrical or plumbing, the contractor may need to upgrade those systems before the project can continue. Hidden noncompliant conditions can add cost, extend the schedule, and require revised permits or inspections.
